full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 10-11-94 and 17-11-94 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Family Appeal No. 7 of 1992 affirming those dated 30-3-92 and 1-4-92 respectively passed by the Additional Assistant Judge-in-Charge and Family Court, Sadar, Chandpur in Family Court Case No. 4 of 1991 should not be set aside. 

 4. The suit was decreed declaring the talak-e-tawfiz exercised by the defendant petitioner is illegal and void and also passed a direction upon the petitioner to establish the conjugal life. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied the petitioner preferred an appeal before the District Judge and the appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge who by this judgment and decree dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the Assistant Judge. 

 5. Both the Courts found that the notice under section 7 read with section 8 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 was not a valid notice and also found that the marriage was still valid and decreed the suit and directed the parties to start with the conjugal life. 

 6. The sole question that was resolved by the Courts below as to whether the notice of divorce sent to the Chairman, Dhaka City Corporation with a copy to the plaintiff was valid or not. In the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 section 7(1) provides that notice has to be served upon the Chairman but instead of serving the notice upon the Chairman of the Union Parishad it was served upon the Chairman, Dhaka City Corporation. It was contended on behalf of the plaintiff that the notice has to be served upon the Chairman of the Union Council. It is held by the Subordinate Judge that the plaintiff did not appear to have lived in the City of Dhaka. Notice under section 7(1) was not validly served. Since the plaintiff and the defendant's marriage still subsisting the plaintiff is entitled to a decree. The learned Judge observed that upon necessary modification of the provision of section the wife while wants to exercise her right to divorce she should serve notice upon the husband where he lives. The learned Judge then referred to the fact that on 5-1-91 the wife divorced her husband her husband did not live at Dhaka as such notice was not properly served but it appears from paragraphs 5 and 6 of the plaint that the plaintiff and the defendant used to live at Tejkunipara, Dhaka and the defendant-wife went away from the said house to her father's village house. The plaintiff while he was waiting for his wife all on a sudden received the talaqnama dated 20-1-91 and was very much surprised. Section 7(1)(2)(3)(4) of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 reads as follows: 

 7. The suit filed by the plaintiff-husband is also for restitution of conjugal right which has been decreed by the Courts below. In the case of Nelly Zaman vs Giasuddin, 34 DLR 221 it has been held that in a suit for restitution of conjugal right and also for declaration that the divorce pronounced by the wife is illegal such direction for restitution of conjugal right as consequential relief is wrong and unenforceable in law. Such direction in matters of relationship between man and wife no longer holds good and is opposed to the principles laid down in Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. Therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below appears not to be tenable in law and, as such, are liable to be set aside. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the judgment and decree dated 10-11-94 and 17-11-94 respectively passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Family Appeal No. 7 of 1992 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-3-92 and 1-4-92 respectively passed by the Additional Assistant Judge-in-Charge and Family Court Sadar, Chandpur in Family Court Case No. 4 of 1991 are hereby set aside. The suit is accordingly dismissed.
